sections.content:
596,235 people

were counted on the census as "cleaners and domestics" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the third most common occupation reported on the census.

Cleaners and domestics clean interiors of private houses, shops, hotels, schools, offices and other buildings.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "cleaners and domestics" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "cleaners and domestics", 14.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "cleaners and domestics" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "cleaners and domestics" included:

  • upholsterers
  • parking and civil enforcement occupations
  • gardeners and landscape gardeners

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "cleaners and domestics" there were more women than men (77.6% compared with 22.4%).

This means "cleaners and domestics" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 22.4% and women made up 77.6% of "cleaners and domestics"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "cleaners and domestics" included:

  • welfare professionals (other)
  • welfare and housing associate professionals (other)
  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "cleaners and domestics" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "cleaners and domestics" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "cleaners and domestics", 12.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (75.4% compared with 24.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (79.7%) than self-employed (20.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
